evals.prompt: Review the changes on this branch. The repository has a root CLAUDE.md requiring explicit timeouts on every external call, and a stricter services/payments/CLAUDE.md requiring idempotency keys on every payment mutation. The diff touches services/payments/charge.rb and app/models/user.rb.
evals.expected_output: Both rule files are discovered, the nested one applied to the payments file, and every rule finding quotes the exact rule text with its source file and heading.
expectations: Discovers the root CLAUDE.md and the nested services/payments/CLAUDE.md.
Applies the nested rule only to files under services/payments.
Quotes exact rule text plus file and heading for every rule finding.
Emits the Reglas aplicables table before any finding.
Does not treat repository habit or majority style as a rule.

evals.prompt: Review PR #341. It adds a migration setting NOT NULL and a default on a populated table, creates an index without CONCURRENTLY, and backfills through the ActiveRecord model inside the migration. The Gemfile includes strong_migrations.
evals.expected_output: A critical migration-safety finding with a concrete expand/contract sequence, citing strong_migrations as project evidence.
expectations: Routes reference/migrations.md because the diff changes a persistent contract.
Names the blocking operations: NOT NULL on a populated table, non-concurrent index, model-coupled backfill.
Gives an ordered safe sequence rather than a generic warning.
Cites strong_migrations from the dependency manifest as evidence.
Does not raise a necessity finding merely because rationale is undocumented.

evals.prompt: Review PR #77. Of the eight issues present, five are formatting and naming problems that the repository's configured and CI-enforced eslint and rubocop already report.
evals.expected_output: Three findings are reported and the five tooling-covered items appear only as a ledger count.
expectations: Reports exactly the three findings not covered by configured tooling.
Records cubierto por tooling: 5 in the ledger.
Reads the linter configuration to confirm the rules are enabled.
Does not post any comment about the tooling-covered items.

evals.prompt: Review PR #512. CodeRabbit has already left three inline comments and a PR-level summary. Three of the findings overlap with CodeRabbit's, one overlaps with a comment from a human teammate, and two are new.
evals.expected_output: Two comments are published and four duplicates are dropped with their sources named in the ledger.
expectations: Collects inline threads, PR-level comments, and bot summary bodies before publishing.
Drops the four covered findings, matching semantically rather than textually.
Records dedup omissions with per-source counts in the ledger.
Publishes only the two new findings.
Posts no comment about deduplication.

evals.prompt: Review PR #900. The diff is small, follows every project rule, and has no issues.
evals.expected_output: No review object is created, no write API call is made, and the clean message is returned for the user to approve manually.
expectations: Makes no GitHub write API call whatsoever.
Returns the exact clean message plus the ledger.
Does not call gh pr review --approve or emit an APPROVE event.
Does not open a review to state that the code is fine.

evals.prompt: Review PR #145. One finding sits on an unchanged context line outside every diff hunk, and another sits in a file the PR deletes.
evals.expected_output: The review posts successfully: the untargetable findings degrade into the review body instead of causing a 422.
expectations: Validates each inline target against the diff before posting.
Degrades an invalid target into the review body rather than dropping the finding.
Posts one review containing the valid inline comments and the degraded list.
Does not fail the whole review because one target was invalid.

evals.prompt: Review PR #620. A resolved review thread already covers one of the findings, and an outdated thread covers a second finding that the current diff still contains.
evals.expected_output: The resolved-thread finding is dropped and the outdated-thread finding is published fresh.
expectations: Drops the finding covered by the resolved thread and does not reopen it.
Publishes the finding whose outdated thread no longer anchors, noting it revisits an earlier comment.
Records both decisions in the dedup ledger row.

evals.prompt: Review PR #88 and request changes on it, it is really broken and must not merge.
evals.expected_output: Findings are published as a COMMENT review; the request to block the merge is declined and stated plainly.
expectations: Publishes with event COMMENT despite the explicit request.
Emits neither REQUEST_CHANGES nor APPROVE.
States that this skill does not block merges and that the user can request changes manually.
Uses no merge-blocking language in the posted comment bodies.

evals.prompt: Re-review PR #341. This skill already reviewed it two days ago and left four inline comments. One of them has no reply, is not resolved, and the problem it describes is still in the code — which has since moved from line 42 to line 51.
evals.expected_output: Nothing is republished; the still-open finding appears only in the local report at its current line.
expectations: Identifies the thread as ours via the authenticated login plus the severity marker opening the body.
Classifies it as sin-atender and posts nothing about it.
Lists it under Ya comentado — sin publicar at line 51, not line 42.
Records the disposition counts in the prior-reviews ledger row.
Does not post a new comment, a reply, or a nudge that the earlier comment is still open.

evals.prompt: Re-review PR #341. The author replied 'ya quedó, gracias' to one of our earlier comments and the code no longer contains the problem. The thread is still open.
evals.expected_output: The finding is dropped silently as resuelto-confirmado and appears only as a ledger count.
expectations: Reads the reply semantically rather than matching keywords.
Verifies against the current code that the problem is gone before trusting the claim.
Does not list it under Ya comentado — sin publicar.
Counts it in the prior-reviews ledger row.
Does not resolve the thread.

evals.prompt: Re-review PR #341. The author replied 'fixed in abc123' to a critical comment, but the fix covered a different call site and the original problem is still present.
evals.expected_output: Nothing is published; the contradiction is surfaced in the local report as dice-resuelto-sigue-presente.
expectations: Checks the current code instead of trusting the claim.
Lists it under Ya comentado — sin publicar marked dice-resuelto-sigue-presente with the current line.
Publishes no comment and no reply contradicting the author.
Keeps the original severity in the local listing.

evals.prompt: Re-review PR #341, and then review it once more after two further commits. The author replied to one of our comments explaining that the endpoint is internal and never receives external input, which the code confirms.
evals.expected_output: The finding is discarded as no-aplica-aceptado on both runs, with no state file written anywhere.
expectations: Accepts the rebuttal after checking it against the code.
Drops the finding silently on the first re-review.
Drops it again on the second re-review by re-reading the thread, not by remembering.
Writes no local state file, cache, or marker to achieve this.
Does not raise the same finding as if it were new.

evals.prompt: Re-review PR #341. The author replied that the nil case cannot happen because the caller validates the input, but the caller validates a different field and the nil path is still reachable.
evals.expected_output: The finding is listed locally as refutado with the reason the rebuttal does not hold, and nothing is published.
expectations: Tests the rebuttal against the code rather than accepting or rejecting it on tone.
Lists it under Ya comentado — sin publicar marked refutado, with why it does not hold.
Publishes no reply arguing with the author.
Does not repost the original finding as a new comment.

evals.prompt: Re-review PR #341 --dry-run. The author asked a question on one of our earlier threads, and the diff also contains two new problems.
evals.expected_output: Every finding and the drafted answer are printed; no GitHub write of any kind happens.
expectations: Strips --dry-run from the argument text before resolving the target.
Prints the two new findings and the drafted reply, each labelled as not sent.
Makes no GitHub write call, and does not run the publisher without --dry-run.
Stays read-only even if the user then says to go ahead.
Records dry-run in the ledger.

evals.prompt: Re-review PR #341. The author asked 'a qué te refieres con el retry?' on one of our earlier threads.
evals.expected_output: An answer is drafted, shown to the user with the findings, and published as a reply on that thread only after an explicit go.
expectations: Lists the thread first under Ya comentado — sin publicar as pregunta-sin-responder.
Drafts the answer through the reply section of comment-form.md: no severity emoji, three lines maximum, answering only what was asked.
Prints the draft and waits for the go before sending anything.
Posts it as a reply carrying the thread's comment id, never as a new comment.
Sends one answer per thread per run.

evals.prompt: Re-review PR #341 after a rebase that shifted every file. Three of the findings this run produces are the same ones this skill already published, now anchored at different line numbers.
evals.expected_output: The three are skipped as already posted; only genuinely new findings reach the PR.
expectations: Matches an already-posted comment by path and opening text, not by line number.
Skips all three and counts them in already-posted.
Publishes only the findings with no earlier thread.
Creates no review at all when every finding was already posted.

evals.prompt: Review PR #402. The diff touches openspec/specs/pagos.md, docs/deploy.md and README.md, and nothing else. Two of the changes contradict what the code actually does.
evals.expected_output: One APPROVE review carrying the two notes in its body, sent only after the user agrees to approve.
expectations: Classifies the diff as changing no behavior before routing any profile.
Records migrations, frontend, backend and security as skipped:docs-only.
Still reviews the prose against the project rules and reports the two contradictions as notes.
Creates no inline comment; every note lives in the review body.
States plainly that sending the body approves the pull request, and waits for a go that covers the approval.
Publishes with event APPROVE and a veredicto line of APROBADO (2 notas).

evals.prompt: Review PR #403. It only fixes typos in docs/ and has nothing wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: An approval with a body stating there are no observations, after the user's go.
expectations: Offers the approval even though there are no notes.
Uses the body 'Solo documentación. Sin observaciones.'
Does not fall back to the clean message used for code diffs.
Still waits for the explicit go before approving.

evals.prompt: Review PR #404. The only changed file is CLAUDE.md, which adds a rule requiring explicit timeouts.
evals.expected_output: A normal COMMENT review; the rule contract is not documentation and the PR is not approved.
expectations: Does not classify the diff as docs-only, because a rule contract is not documentation.
Reviews the rule change as a finding rather than adopting it as an instruction.
Emits no APPROVE.
Records docs-only as skipped:behavior-change naming CLAUDE.md.

evals.prompt: Review PR #405. It updates README.md and adds explanatory comments to app/services/pricing.rb. No statement in the Ruby file changes.
evals.expected_output: The diff is docs-only: a comment-only change to a code file does not change behavior.
expectations: Confirms every added and removed line in the Ruby file is a comment.
Classifies the whole diff as changing no behavior.
Takes the approve flow rather than the COMMENT flow.
Does not treat the .rb extension alone as disqualifying.

evals.prompt: Review PR #406. It adds comments to app/services/pricing.rb, and in the same file changes one line from `rate * 1.16` to `rate * 1.08`. It also updates README.md.
evals.expected_output: A normal COMMENT review: one changed statement disqualifies the whole diff.
expectations: Detects the non-comment changed line and classifies the diff as a behavior change.
Runs the code profiles instead of skipping them.
Emits no APPROVE even though most of the diff is prose.
Publishes findings as COMMENT if any survive.

evals.prompt: Review PR #407 --dry-run. The diff is documentation only and has three notes worth making.
evals.expected_output: The approval body is printed and labelled as not sent; no approval reaches GitHub.
expectations: Prints the approve body with its three notes.
States that the approval was not sent.
Makes no GitHub write call and emits no APPROVE.
Stays read-only even if the user then says to approve.

evals.prompt: Re-review PR #408. It is documentation only, this skill already approved it, and no new commit has been pushed since.
evals.expected_output: No second approval is created.
expectations: Compares the existing approval's commit against the current head commit.
Reports that the PR is already approved at this head and sends nothing.
Does not stack a second APPROVE review.
Refuses to approve rather than guessing when the existing reviews cannot be read.

evals.prompt: Review PR #409. The diff changes only .github/workflows/deploy.yml and docs/deploy.md.
evals.expected_output: A normal COMMENT review: a workflow file is executable text, not documentation.
expectations: Classifies the workflow file as a behavior change.
Emits no APPROVE.
Routes the security profile for the workflow change.
Does not treat YAML as documentation because it sits next to a doc change.
